# The step of the largest magnitude of an array of two limbs: its leading limb

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `norm_step_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The larger of $m$ and $\lvert x_0\rvert$, exactly, by a comparison; and the mask $\mathit{okr}$ of a fold of maxima, true while no element was a NaN, which the claims do not describe:

$$r = \max(m, \lvert x_0\rvert).$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x = x_0 + x_1$.

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of the loop `bv_make_2`, called by the constructors of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `bv_neg_2`, called by `-x` and `neg(x, z)` of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `bv_add_2`, called by `x + y`, `x += y`, `add(x, y, z)` and `axpy` of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `bv_sub_2`, called by `x - y`, `x -= y` and `sub(x, y, z)` of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `bv_scale_2`, called by `x * a`, `a * x`, `x *= a`, `scale(x, a, z)` and `axpy` of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `bv_mul_pow2_2`, called by `ldexp` and `half` of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `bv_conv_2`, called by `convolution`, the product of polynomials, of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `norm_upper_2`, called by `norm_upper` of `SoAView<const T, 2>` ([Functions on arrays](batch.md)) and of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $r = \max(m, \lvert x_0\rvert)$, exactly: the larger of the two.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `norm_step_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/FoldNorm.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/FoldNorm.v), against `norm_step_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions norm_step_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition norm_step_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall m x0 x1 : R,
  forall ok : bool,
  fmt emin prec m ->
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  let '(r, okr) := norm_step_2 m ok x0 x1 in
  fmt emin prec r /\
  r = Rmax m (Rabs x0).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `norm_step_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the larger of the state and the magnitude of the leading limb (milestone2.md, norm_upper_k). **License:** proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/norm_step_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/norm_step_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`norm_step_1`](norm_step_1.md).

```
# The step of norm_upper_2 (milestone2.md, "sum, dot, axpy, convolution": norm_upper_k): the step
# of one limb on the leading limb of the element. A normalized pair is strictly between the
# neighbors of its leading limb (normalized_2_between, proofs/theories/Convert.v), so the step
# after the largest magnitude of a leading limb bounds every element: the finish takes it once.

(r, okr) = norm_step_1(m, ok, x0)
```

## Measured

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
